summary: Radar for 2026-11-06, GLP-1 focus, built around Lane A. The biggest openings are practical tirzepatide questions with a fresh news hook. (1) Injection site reactions has been in 11 snapshots and its momentum keeps rising (72→85), and its Short reached 226 views by day 3. It's the clearest next long-form. (2) Thanksgiving peaks Nov 18–27. (3) The 'sick day / ER' and dehydration cluster got a fresh hook from 'ER Doctor: What GLP-1 users need to know' (Nov 5), just as cold and flu season starts. (4) Washington Poison Center GLP-1 calls (KING5, KIRO, MyNorthwest, Nov 4–6) open a calm 'took an extra dose by mistake?' reassurance Short. The context is the national poison-centre data (HealthDay and Drug Topics, June–July 2026). (5) Vitamin/B12 and nutrient worries came back with FOX Carolina (Nov 5) and a Cureus Wernicke case report (Nov 5). We frame it as 'eat for nutrients on tirzepatide', not fear. Fresh randomized hooks for 13:00 Shorts: TOGETHER-PsA 52-week tirzepatide plus ixekizumab at ACR Convergence (43.7% vs 15.7% ACR50), and REDEFINE 4 (CagriSema vs tirzepatide) at ObesityWeek Nov 14–17. REDEFINE 4 is the only likely trigger for an extra L2 head-to-head long-form within 48 h of release. Also emerging: NSAIDs and GI bleeding on GLP-1s (AJHP, Nov 5); semaglutide/tirzepatide and alcohol-related outcomes (target-trial emulation, DOM Nov 3), with a holiday-drinking hook; the over-65 cluster (WRAL Nov 5, JAMA frailty); and the Wegovy pill's Australian approval. For that last one we compare with tirzepatide using a 'separate trials' framing. Rejected: the Stanford 'natural Ozempic' BRP story (a 2025 Nature paper on mice and minipigs, repackaged), the Forbes piece on retatrutide online sales, teen gray-market stories, and every cost, telehealth or GoodRx plan story. Verification notes: I couldn't open the NSAID abstract (PubMed showed only a cookie wall), so the scriptwriter must pull the numbers from the PubMed record. The Washington-specific 'tripled' figure is only in the news headlines. National data confirm the trend.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide injection site reactions: what's normal (redness, itching, small lumps), what the label reports, and when to call your prescriber
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, 'worried → answered'. Open with you finding a small red itchy patch the day after your shot. Cover what the label reports vs placebo, why it happens, which reactions are typical and which signs mean call your prescriber (spreading redness, warmth, pus, fever, signs of allergy). End with simple, non-dosing comfort habits: let the pen reach room temperature, rotate sites as the instructions describe, don't rub. Link to Side Effects.

candidates.topic: Took an extra tirzepatide dose by mistake? What poison centers are seeing, and who to call
candidates.angle: Calm 08:00 body-worry Short: 'Is it dangerous if I accidentally inject twice?' Poison centers report more GLP-1 calls, often from dosing mix-ups. Main effects: nausea and vomiting, sometimes low blood sugar (higher risk with insulin or sulfonylureas). Who to call: US Poison Help 1-800-222-1222, or your local poison or emergency number in the UK, Canada and Australia, plus your prescriber. Give no dosing instructions, and don't mention compounded vials or name sources.
candidates.why_now: KING5, KIRO 7 and MyNorthwest (Nov 4–6) report Washington Poison Center GLP-1 calls nearly tripling or doubling, building on the 2026 national poison-centre data (HealthDay, June; Drug Topics, July). People search for this in a panic, and few calm answers exist.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide plus ixekizumab for psoriatic arthritis with obesity: TOGETHER-PsA 52-week results at ACR Convergence 2026
candidates.angle: 13:00 fresh-randomized Short with tirzepatide named first: 'Can tirzepatide help arthritis pain?' At week 52, 43.7% on ixekizumab plus tirzepatide reached ACR50 vs 15.7% on ixekizumab alone, in adults with active PsA and overweight or obesity. Phase 3b, company-funded. State that the combination isn't approved for this use. Weight loss is one piece of joint health.
